attribution.note: Marcus's own aside in his own post. The quoted AI 2027 text is separate; the GPT-5 remark is his.

semantics.note: A faithful retrospective observation: GPT-5 was not yet out and the wait had run well over two years. The revision correctly drops wording he did not use.

contract.note: Marcus did not say when the wait began. Counting from GPT-4's public release is the ordinary reading. Reading 'well over' as months past two years is fair, though a margin of about two months is near the low end.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own release note dates GPT-4's release to Mar 14, 2023. That puts the post date about 2 years, 2 months later.
Contemporary reporting from April 7, 2025 says GPT-5 was delayed and still awaited, which falls inside the target period.
OpenAI's launch post is dated Aug 7, 2025, before the evaluation date. It shows GPT-5 first arrived after the post, which implies it was unreleased on May 22. The drafter labelled it context.

reviews.rationale: GPT-4 was released Mar 14, 2023. GPT-5 was still delayed in April 2025 and launched Aug 7, 2025, so it was unreleased on May 22, 2025, about 26 months after GPT-4. That fits 'well over two years' on the contract's fair plain reading. Internal development time is not established, but the contract reasonably does not require it.
